title: 2026-10-28 Sovereign / interpretive Aramaic-sensitive Lord's Prayer / Genesis side FINAL
sourceNotes: Peshitta Syriac Aramaic is a historical witness, not verifiable verbatim Galilean Aramaic.
Neil Douglas-Klotz Prayers of the Cosmos is interpretive poetic inspiration, not the exact lexical meaning of the Syriac.
Literal Greek/Syriac senses retained where practical; inner insight, purpose, mistakes binding, unripeness, surface delusion are intentional interpretive expansions.
King of Judeans historical inscriptions and political quotations are unchanged; God already Sovereign in previous editorial release.
Genesis side stage is LAST for current public canonical release and most recent public change-log entry.

sovereign.original: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, 'Come, blessed of my Cosmic Parent, inherit the reign prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
sovereign.final: Then the Sovereign will tell those on his right hand, 'Come, blessed of my Cosmic Parent, inherit the reign prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
sovereign.rationale: Yeshua identified as the Human One in 25:31. Greek basileus means king; Sovereign is intentional TWV interpretive authority title, not removal of a God reference.

sovereign.original: "The King will answer them, 'Most certainly I tell you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.'
sovereign.final: "The Sovereign will answer them, 'Most certainly I tell you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.'
sovereign.rationale: Identical christological referent to 25:34; preserve brothers pending separate adelphoi review.

sovereign.original: These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Master of masters, and King of kings. They also will overcome who are with him, called and chosen and faithful."
sovereign.final: These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Master of masters, and Sovereign of sovereigns. They also will overcome who are with him, called and chosen and faithful."
sovereign.rationale: Greek kyrios/masters and basileus/kings each retained conceptually while aligning Yeshua sovereign title.

sovereign.original: He has on his garment and on his thigh a name written, "KING OF KINGS AND SOVEREIGN OF SOVEREIGNS."
sovereign.final: He has on his garment and on his thigh a name written, "SOVEREIGN OF SOVEREIGNS AND MASTER OF MASTERS."
sovereign.rationale: Greek basileus basileon kai kyrios kyrion source order restored; TWV Sovereign for basileus, Master for kyrios.

prayer.original: Pray, then, in this way: "Our Cosmic Parent in the heavens, let your living name be made holy."
prayer.final: Pray, then, in this way: "Our Cosmic Parent in the heavens, may your name be held holy, and your presence awaken within us and shine through the way we live.
prayer.rationale: Greek/syriac holy name retained; awakening and lived radiance are interpretation not lexical equivalence.

prayer.original: Let your reign of unity come. Let your desire be done, as in the heavens, so also on earth.
prayer.final: May your reign of unity grow among us. May your purpose take shape through our hearts and willing hands, on earth as in the heavens.
prayer.rationale: Greek basileia and thelema/Syriac malkutha and sebyana support reign and will/desire; unity/participation are spiritual interpretation.

prayer.original: Give us today our daily bread and insight for the way.
prayer.final: Give us today the bread we need, the insight to understand our way, and nourishment to grow into our purpose.
prayer.rationale: Bread needed/daily grounded in Greek epiousios and Syriac d-sunqanan; insight/purpose are interpretive expansions.

prayer.original: Release us from our debts, as we also release our debtors.
prayer.final: Release us from the debts and mistakes that bind us, as we release others from what we hold against them.
prayer.rationale: Greek opheilemata debts retained; mistakes/binding are pastoral explanatory expansions (Douglas-Klotz inspired).

prayer.original: Do not let us enter the trial that is too great for us, but free us from what has gone sour and corrupt in us and around us. For yours is the reign, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.'
prayer.final: Do not let surface things delude us or the trials of life cause us to lose our way. Free us from unripeness, from harm within and around us, and from all that holds us back from becoming whole. For yours is the reign, the power, and the glory, from age to age. Amen.'
prayer.rationale: Testing and evil source senses preserved in trials/harm; surface delusion, unripeness and wholeness are poetic resonance, not directly Syriac lexemes. Doxology retained as textual/liturgical variant, flagged for notes.

prayer.original: He said to them, "When you pray, say: Our Cosmic Parent in the heavens, let your name be made holy. Let your reign come.
prayer.final: He said to them, "When you pray, say: Our Cosmic Parent in the heavens, may your name be held holy, and your presence awaken within us and shine through the way we live. May your reign of unity grow among us.
prayer.rationale: Luke's shorter parallel retained; spiritual expansions align with Matthew but distinguish Luke's textual witnesses.

prayer.original: Give us day by day our daily bread.
prayer.final: Give us each day the bread we need, with insight for the way and nourishment to grow in purpose.
prayer.rationale: Daily provision retained; insight/growing purpose are explicitly poetic spiritual application.

prayer.original: Forgive us our moral failures, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. Do not let us enter the trial that is too great for us, but free us from what has gone sour and corrupt in us and around us.'"
prayer.final: Release us from our moral failures and the debts that bind us, for we also release all who are indebted to us. Do not let surface things delude us or testing lead us astray; free us from unripeness, from harm within and around us, and all that holds us back from becoming whole.'"
prayer.rationale: Luke Greek hamartias/sins and indebted people preserved. Longer deliverance clause in this TWV textual tradition; interpretive material disclosed.

rib.original: YHWH Elohim caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As he slept, YHWH Elohim took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
rib.final: YHWH Elohim caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As he slept, YHWH Elohim took one of his sides, and closed up the flesh in its place.
rib.rationale: Hebrew tsela more broadly side; rib possible narrower sense but not certain. Preserve October 15 man/human decision and sleep/flesh imagery.

rib.original: YHWH Elohim made a woman from the rib which YHWH Elohim had taken from the man, and brought her to him.
rib.final: YHWH Elohim fashioned the side that had been taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to him.
rib.rationale: Hebrew tsela side; banah conveys building/fashioning. 'Eve' naming is later, Genesis 3:20.
